column3: The Hebrew explicitly repeats the LORD’s name and does not explicitly say “Again”; BSB uses “He” for the second divine name and supplies “Again.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses singular collective “Israel,” names Midian and Amalek, and calls the eastern people “sons of the east”; BSB uses plural people names and supplies “other.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective names for the sheep, ox, and donkey; BSB has plural “sheep,” “oxen,” and “donkeys.”
The Hebrew begins with “they”; BSB explicitly names “the Midianites.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD as sender and separately says He brought them up and brought them out; BSB begins with “He” and combines the two actions into “brought you up out.”
The Hebrew repeats singular “hand” for Egypt and all the oppressors; BSB uses plural “hands” once.
The Hebrew has singular collective “the Amorite” and explicitly names “My voice”; BSB has plural “Amorites” and “obey Me.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the angel appeared “to him”; BSB explicitly names Gideon.
The Hebrew says these things “found us” and names the palm of Midian; BSB has “happened to us” and “the hand of Midian.”
The Hebrew says “this strength of yours” and uses a completed sending verb in the question; BSB has “the strength you have” and “Am I not sending you?”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and calls the clan “my thousand”; BSB names Gideon and says “my clan.”
The Hebrew names Midian without an explicit “all”; BSB says “all the Midianites.”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and says “in your eyes”; BSB names Gideon and says “in Your sight.”
The Hebrew leaves the second speaker unnamed; BSB explicitly names the LORD.
The Hebrew describes unleavened bread made from an ephah of flour; BSB coordinates the bread and “an ephah of flour” with “and.”
The Hebrew says “he did so”; BSB explicitly names Gideon.
The Hebrew says the angel “went from his eyes”; BSB says he “vanished from his sight.”
The Hebrew repeats Gideon’s name as the speaker; BSB uses “he.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew refers to the person addressed as “him”; BSB names Gideon.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the bull was offered on “the built altar” without an explicit word “newly”; BSB supplies “newly.”
The Hebrew repeats “this thing” in the question and answer and actively says “they said”; BSB uses “this” and “it” and the passive “they were told.”
The Hebrew repeats “because” for demolishing the altar and cutting the Asherah; BSB states the reason once for both actions.
